subject: Meridian Labs: DPA Annex, DPF Evidence & Regional Routing Options
messages:
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@meridianlabs.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Meridian Procurement <procurement@meridianlabs.com>
Date: 2025-08-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Meridian Labs: DPA Annex, DPF evidence and routing requirements

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Procurement and our security team have a few follow-up requests to keep our timeline — we need to complete legal and technical review by Aug 30. Can you please provide the following by COB Aug 25 if possible: 

1) A canonical DPA annex (trackable PDF) that we can circulate to legal (we may propose a few redlines).
2) A current subprocessor inventory (CSV) with locations and whether subprocessors have access to plaintext customer data.
3) Technical evidence for cross-border transfer protections (DPF-like evidence): routing controls, KV/prefix caching behavior, and whether requests from EU customers can be pinned to EU-only processing.
4) Confirmation of KMS/HSM options (BYOK supported? customer-managed keys?).
5) Any constraints or changes if we want EU-residency and support for EU-only logging/retention.

A couple of clarifying notes from security: they want an explicit description of the fallback behavior (if EU capacity is saturated, will requests fall back to non-EU regions?) and whether that can be disabled for a subset of routes.

Can you confirm what you can provide and a proposed delivery date? Happy to schedule a 30-min call with security next week.

Best,
Aisha Khan
Sr. Procurement Manager | Meridian Labs

Attachments: none

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@meridianlabs.com>
Cc: Meridian Procurement <procurement@meridianlabs.com>
Date: 2025-08-19T12:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Meridian Labs: DPA Annex, DPF evidence and routing requirements

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear list. We can provide everything you asked for. High-level answers here and we will follow with a package and a short security readout by Aug 22: 

- Canonical DPA annex: yes — I will attach redwood_dpa_annex_v2.pdf and include a one-page summary of change areas.
- Subprocessor inventory: CSV will include region, purpose, and access level.
- Cross-border protections / DPF evidence: we have a technical evidence readme that explains routing policies, per-route pinning, and fallback configuration. We’ll include examples for Dedicated and Private deployments for EU-only residency.
- KMS/HSM: BYOK is supported for Private; for Dedicated we support customer-managed keys via our KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and hardware-backed HSM for Private deployments — details in the attached readme.
- Fallback behavior: by default requests will failover to compatible regions for availability; we can support an enforcement policy to block non-EU routing for specified routes (this is a configuration we apply at provisioning).

Two quick clarifying Qs before we prepare the package:
1) Do you need EU-residency for all request/response content, or only for logs/retention?
2) Are you evaluating Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated capacity, or Private (VPC/on-prem)? This affects the evidence we provide.

If you prefer, we can do a 30-min technical review on Aug 24 or 25. I’ll loop in our product security and ops owners.

Thanks — STEPH

--
Stephanie Nguyen
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: Meridian Labs: DPA Annex, DPF evidence and routing requirements — package ready for review

Steph / Karthik / Jordan — draft package ready for internal review. Attachments here: redwood_dpa_annex_v2.pdf (canonical annex), subprocessor_inventory_2025-08.csv, dpf_technical_evidence_readme.txt. Quick highlights for Meridian: 

- EU-residency options: Hosted + region pinning (best-effort), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools in EU region with per-route pinning), Private (customer-managed VPC/on-prem with full residency). We document the trade-offs in the readme.
- Fallback enforcement: we implemented an enforcement flag at the route level ("enforce_residency": true) that prevents non-EU routing and returns 429/503 rather than auto-failover. This is available for Dedicated and Private; Hosted can be configured for best-effort and alerts on capacity issues.
- KMS/HSM: BYOK supported for Dedicated via KMS integration; Private supports customer HSM (YubiHSM/Tang style) — noted in the annex and readme.
- Subprocessors: list includes infra providers, monitoring vendors, and certain model hosting partners. Each row in the CSV indicates whether the subprocessor processes plaintext customer payloads.

I flagged three items for legal: clauses referencing indemnity and export control language (Jordan).

If internal review good, I will send to Meridian with a short cover email and DocuSign link for the DPA annex.

--
Marissa Cole
Platform Privacy Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments (stubs): redwood_dpa_annex_v2.pdf, subprocessor_inventory_2025-08.csv, dpf_technical_evidence_readme.txt

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@meridianlabs.com>, Meridian Procurement <procurement@meridianlabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-22T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Meridian Labs: DPA Annex + DPF evidence package (attachments + next steps)

Hi Aisha — attaching the package as requested. Summary below and next steps at the bottom.

Attachments (stubs):
- redwood_dpa_annex_v2.pdf — canonical DPA annex with editable sections called out (Jordan has flagged export-control language for discussion).
- subprocessor_inventory_2025-08.csv — rows: subprocessor name, region(s), role, plaintext_access (yes/no), attestation links.
- dpf_technical_evidence_readme.txt — routing, caching, KV, policy enforcement, and example config for Dedicated/Private/Hosted.

Direct answers to your bullets: 
1) EU-residency: We can provide EU-only processing and logging via Dedicated and Private deployments. Hosted can be configured with region pinning but is best-effort for availability; we offer an enforcement flag to block non-EU routing for a route.
2) Subprocessor detail: See CSV. Any subprocessor that has plaintext access is marked; most platform infra vendors do not access customer plaintext.
3) Cross-border evidence: the readme includes diagrams and configuration examples for request routing, KV/prefix caching behavior, and automated fallbacks.
4) KMS/HSM: BYOK supported for Dedicated (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and full HSM options for Private deployments. We can include an HSM attestation for Private upon request.
5) Fallback policy: enforcement flag available to deny non-EU processing on a per-route basis (returns 429 or configurable error). Default Hosted behavior is to failover for availability.

Next steps:
- If legal wants to redline the annex, please return comments to Jordan (jordan.blake@redwood.com). We can iterate quickly.
- We have placed the DPA annex in DocuSign for signature if you prefer the standard form: https://docusign.com/XYZ/meridian-dpa
- Proposed security review call: Aug 25 at 10:00 AM BST / Aug 24 US-friendly options. Tell me preferred slot and we’ll invite our infra/product security owners.

If you want a tighter EU-only SLA, we can propose Dedicated capacity with reserved GPU pools in the EU region — I can provide a costing addendum.

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
